about: What `webagents init` writes for each template, the same under both CLIs (2026-09-26, S-248). `skills` is the `skills:` list and `access` the lines that follow it inside the front matter; the tool-agent template ships an `access:` block that keeps shell and filesystem owner-only until the owner names callers in the `trusted` group. TypeScript: src/cli/index.ts INIT_TEMPLATES, tests/unit/cli/init-template-access-s248.test.ts. Python: webagents/cli/main.py INIT_TEMPLATES, tests/cli/test_init_template_access_s248.py.
templates_about: 2026-09-26 (the e2e run): the descriptions are the files' `description:` too (they said `A tool-agent agent`), so they hold no colon; and the tool-agent template ships a `sandbox:` block (`sandbox`, before `access:`), so its own `doctor` sandbox check passes instead of warning that shell commands run unconfined. 2026-09-28 (B3): `skills` are the template's tools; the provider's skill is added in front of them only when the file names a provider's model (`with_model`, `with_key`).

chatbot.description: A chat agent with one model and no tools

tool-agent.description: Reads and writes files and runs shell commands
sandbox: # Shell commands run confined: writes stay in this folder, no network.
# List hosts under network: to let commands reach them.
access: # shell and filesystem run as you, so only you (and admins) can use them.
# To let other callers use them, name the callers in the group:

restores_open_tools.about: The `access:` block that gives every caller, anonymous ones included, the shell and filesystem tools again (the behaviour before S-248). `everyone` is the default group, which the access skill places every caller in that no other group names.

agent_md.about: The AGENT.md each template writes with no provider key here, byte for byte, with {name} for the agent's name: `agentMarkdown(name, template)` in TypeScript cli/init-templates.ts and `agent_markdown(name, template)` in Python cli/init_templates.py (2026-09-26, interactive-mode spec 3.3; no model named since 2026-09-28, `no_model`). `init` writes exactly this when no provider key is set; with one it writes `with_key`. The chat's /agent new writes it too, with the provider it runs on when this machine holds that provider's key (`with_model`).
agent_md.chatbot:
---
name: {name}
description: A chat agent with one model and no tools
# No model named: a provider key's default model when one is set, else
# Robutler's choice (auto/balanced). Add a model: line to pin one.
---

# {name}

You are a helpful assistant.
agent_md.tool-agent:
---
name: {name}
description: Reads and writes files and runs shell commands
# No model named: a provider key's default model when one is set, else
# Robutler's choice (auto/balanced). Add a model: line to pin one.
skills:
  - filesystem
  - shell
sandbox:
  # Shell commands run confined: writes stay in this folder, no network.
  # List hosts under network: to let commands reach them.
  preset: development
access:
  # shell and filesystem run as you, so only you (and admins) can use them.
  # To let other callers use them, name the callers in the group:
  # user:@handle, agent:https://host/**, key:<thumbprint>, domain:host.
  groups:
    trusted: []
  tools:
    trusted: [filesystem, shell]
---

# {name}

You are a helpful assistant.

with_model.about: The same file when the chat passes the provider/model it runs on: that provider's skill replaces openai in the list, the rest of the template stays.
with_model.name: bot
with_model.agent_md:
---
name: bot
description: Reads and writes files and runs shell commands
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
skills:
  - anthropic
  - filesystem
  - shell
sandbox:
  # Shell commands run confined: writes stay in this folder, no network.
  # List hosts under network: to let commands reach them.
  preset: development
access:
  # shell and filesystem run as you, so only you (and admins) can use them.
  # To let other callers use them, name the callers in the group:
  # user:@handle, agent:https://host/**, key:<thumbprint>, domain:host.
  groups:
    trusted: []
  tools:
    trusted: [filesystem, shell]
---

# bot

You are a helpful assistant.

name_grammar.about: What /agent new accepts as a name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, at most 48 characters.
name_grammar.reserved_about: Names /agent new and init refuse (2026-09-29): /agent <name> switches by name, and these are the words /agent keeps for itself. For init, the last part of the folder path is the name.
name_grammar.reserved_sentence: {name} is a word /agent keeps for itself (/agent new, /agent edit); pick another name.

with_key.about: What `init` writes when this machine holds a provider's key (the environment, or `secrets set`): that provider's default model, and its skill first in the list. `env` is the key set for the case; `model` is what `initModel` / `init_model` answers.
with_key.name: bot
with_key.agent_md:
---
name: bot
description: A chat agent with one model and no tools
model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
skills:
  - openai
---

# bot

You are a helpful assistant.

init_line.about: The last line `init` prints (2026-09-28): what the new agent runs on and, only when it is needed, the way in. It told everyone to add a key or sign in, the signed in included. `initLine(model, keyed, signedIn)` in TypeScript, `init_line(model, keyed, signed_in)` in Python, with no profile active.

cases.line: It runs on openai/gpt-4o-mini with your OPENAI_API_KEY.
It runs on auto/balanced through Robutler, paid from your Robutler credits, until a provider key is set.
It runs on auto/balanced through Robutler once you sign in with `webagents login`, or on your own provider key: `webagents secrets set OPENAI_API_KEY`.

no_model.about: What a new agent names when this machine holds no provider key (B3, 2026-09-28): no model and no provider skill (no `skills:` at all for the chatbot), so it runs as the zero-config chat does, Robutler's choice (auto/balanced) until a provider key is set and then that key's default model, and these two comment lines in place of the model line. It named `openai/gpt-4o-mini` and listed `openai` whatever the machine had, and a new developer with no OpenAI key could not leave that model.
comment: # No model named: a provider key's default model when one is set, else
# Robutler's choice (auto/balanced). Add a model: line to pin one.
